lines.raw: The idea in one sentence.
lines.say: The idea in one sentence.

lines.raw: An **episode of care** is all the care linked to one condition or one procedure, gathered from many claims and providers within a defined time window, so that the **whole treatment** can be costed and compared.
lines.say: An episode of care is all the care linked to one condition or one procedure, gathered from many claims and providers within a defined time window, so that the whole treatment can be costed and compared.

lines.raw: The US version: the parts of an episode definition.
lines.say: The U S version: the parts of an episode definition.

scenes.section: The US version: the parts of an episode definition

lines.raw: Trigger.
lines.say: Trigger.

lines.raw: The claim that starts an episode, for example a hospital stay with a knee replacement DRG, or a knee replacement procedure code on an outpatient claim.
lines.say: The claim that starts an episode, for example a hospital stay with a knee replacement D R G, or a knee replacement procedure code on an outpatient claim.

lines.raw: Pre-trigger window (look-back).
lines.say: Pre-trigger window (look-back).

lines.raw: Days **before** the trigger whose related care is included, for example pre-surgery tests and visits.
lines.say: Days before the trigger whose related care is included, for example pre-surgery tests and visits.

lines.raw: Post-trigger window.
lines.say: Post-trigger window.

lines.raw: Days **after** the trigger (often after hospital discharge) whose related care is included: rehab, follow-up visits, readmissions.
lines.say: Days after the trigger (often after hospital discharge) whose related care is included: rehab, follow-up visits, readmissions.

lines.raw: Clean period.
lines.say: Clean period.

lines.raw: The quiet time used to separate episodes.
lines.say: The quiet time used to separate episodes.

lines.raw: A new trigger only starts a new episode if there was no episode of the same type for the member during the clean period; otherwise its care belongs to the open episode.
lines.say: A new trigger only starts a new episode if there was no episode of the same type for the member during the clean period; otherwise its care belongs to the open episode.

lines.raw: Relatedness rules.
lines.say: Relatedness rules.

lines.raw: Which claims inside the window count: all care ("all-cause"), or only care linked to the condition by diagnosis and procedure lists.
lines.say: Which claims inside the window count: all care ("all-cause"), or only care linked to the condition by diagnosis and procedure lists.

lines.raw: Attribution.
lines.say: Attribution.

lines.raw: Deciding which provider is **responsible** for the episode, for example the hospital where the surgery happened, or the operating surgeon.
lines.say: Deciding which provider is responsible for the episode, for example the hospital where the surgery happened, or the operating surgeon.

scenes.section: The US version: the parts of an episode definition

lines.raw: Three kinds of episode.
lines.say: Three kinds of episode.

lines.raw: **Procedural**. Starts with: A planned procedure. Window: Fixed days before and after. Example: Knee replacement, heart bypass surgery.
lines.say: Procedural. Starts with: A planned procedure. Window: Fixed days before and after. Example: Knee replacement, heart bypass surgery.

lines.raw: **Acute medical**. Starts with: An emergency or sudden illness, usually a hospital admission. Window: Fixed days after discharge. Example: Pneumonia, heart attack.
lines.say: Acute medical. Starts with: An emergency or sudden illness, usually a hospital admission. Window: Fixed days after discharge. Example: Pneumonia, heart attack.

lines.raw: **Chronic**. Starts with: A diagnosis of a long-lasting condition. Window: A fixed period, often a year, renewed while the condition lasts. Example: Diabetes, asthma.
lines.say: Chronic. Starts with: A diagnosis of a long-lasting condition. Window: A fixed period, often a year, renewed while the condition lasts. Example: Diabetes, asthma.

scenes.section: The US version: the parts of an episode definition

lines.raw: Two well-known Medicare episode windows.
lines.say: Two well-known Medicare episode windows.

lines.raw: **MSPB** (Medicare Spending per Beneficiary), a hospital efficiency measure. Trigger: A hospital admission. Window: 3 days before admission to 30 days after discharge.
lines.say: M S P B (Medicare Spending per Beneficiary), a hospital efficiency measure. Trigger: A hospital admission. Window: 3 days before admission to 30 days after discharge.

lines.raw: **CJR** (Comprehensive Care for Joint Replacement), a bundled payment model. Trigger: A hospital stay for hip or knee replacement. Window: The stay plus 90 days after discharge.
lines.say: C J R (Comprehensive Care for Joint Replacement), a bundled payment model. Trigger: A hospital stay for hip or knee replacement. Window: The stay plus 90 days after discharge.

lines.raw: Episodes vs bundled payments.

lines.raw: An episode is an **analysis unit**.
lines.say: An episode is an analysis unit.

lines.raw: A **bundled payment** uses an episode definition to set a target price and share savings or losses with providers.
lines.say: A bundled payment uses an episode definition to set a target price and share savings or losses with providers.

lines.raw: How bundles pay is taught in the Value Based Care course; this course shows how episodes are defined and built from claims.
lines.say: How bundles pay is taught in the Value Based Care course; this course shows how episodes are defined and built from claims.

lines.raw: **Robert** (born 1957, a retired teacher in Houston with type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure, on the made-up Medicare Advantage plan Gulf Coast Advantage) is admitted to Harbor Point Hospital (made up) on **8 September 2025** for a right knee replacement and goes home on **10 September**.
lines.say: Robert (born 1957, a retired teacher in Houston with type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure, on the made-up Medicare Advantage plan Gulf Coast Advantage) is admitted to Harbor Point Hospital (made up) on 8 September 2025 for a right knee replacement and goes home on 10 September.

lines.raw: His plan's analytics team uses this (illustrative) definition:

scenes.section: Worked example: defining Robert's knee replacement episode

lines.raw: Gulf Coast Advantage knee replacement episode definition (illustrative).
lines.say: Gulf Coast Advantage knee replacement episode definition (illustrative).

lines.raw: Trigger. Rule: Inpatient stay grouped to a major knee joint replacement DRG, or outpatient CPT `27447`. For Robert: Stay 8 to 10 September 2025.
lines.say: Trigger. Rule: Inpatient stay grouped to a major knee joint replacement D R G, or outpatient C P T 2 7 4 4 7. For Robert: Stay 8 to 10 September 2025.

lines.raw: Pre-trigger window. Rule: 30 days before admission. For Robert: 9 August to 7 September 2025.
lines.say: Pre-trigger window. Rule: 30 days before admission. For Robert: 9 August to 7 September 2025.

lines.raw: Post-trigger window. Rule: 90 days after discharge. For Robert: 11 September to 9 December 2025.
lines.say: Post-trigger window. Rule: 90 days after discharge. For Robert: 11 September to 9 December 2025.

lines.raw: Clean period. Rule: No knee replacement episode for the same member in the previous 90 days. For Robert: None found: a new episode starts.
lines.say: Clean period. Rule: No knee replacement episode for the same member in the previous 90 days. For Robert: None found: a new episode starts.

lines.raw: Relatedness. Rule: Care with a knee or joint diagnosis, surgical complications, rehab, and any readmission. For Robert: Applied in lesson 7.
lines.say: Relatedness. Rule: Care with a knee or joint diagnosis, surgical complications, rehab, and any readmission. For Robert: Applied in lesson 7.

lines.raw: Attribution. Rule: The hospital where the trigger stay happened. For Robert: Harbor Point Hospital.
lines.say: Attribution. Rule: The hospital where the trigger stay happened. For Robert: Harbor Point Hospital.

lines.raw: Check the dates.
lines.say: Check the dates.

lines.raw: 8 September − 30 days = **9 August**.
lines.say: 8 September − 30 days = 9 August.

lines.raw: 10 September + 90 days = **9 December** (20 days left in September + 31 in October + 30 in November + 9 in December = 90).
lines.say: 10 September and 90 days = 9 December (20 days left in September and 31 in October and 30 in November and 9 in December = 90).

lines.say: A 30-day window and a 90-day window give very different episode costs; "all-cause" includes Robert's routine diabetes check, "related only" does not.

lines.raw: When you compare episode costs, make sure every number used the **same definition**, and write the definition next to the result.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: An episode gathers all care for one condition or procedure across claims and providers within a time window.
lines.say: An episode gathers all care for one condition or procedure across claims and providers within a time window.

lines.raw: An episode definition has a trigger, windows before and after, a clean period, relatedness rules and attribution.
lines.say: An episode definition has a trigger, windows before and after, a clean period, relatedness rules and attribution.

lines.raw: Episodes can be procedural, acute medical or chronic.
lines.say: Episodes can be procedural, acute medical or chronic.

lines.raw: Bundled payments use episode definitions to pay; the Value Based Care course covers that.
lines.say: Bundled payments use episode definitions to pay; the Value Based Care course covers that.

lines.raw: Different definitions give different costs, so compare only like with like.
lines.say: Different definitions give different costs, so compare only like with like.
